# Phase 2.0 — Hermetic replay and the golden harness

The safety net for the renderer work, plus the correctness bug found while building it.
No run stream, no SVG, no tokenizer changes.

**Revision 2.** The first draft rested on a false premise: that `--data` replay is hermetic.
It is not. Every change from that draft is marked **[R]**.

## The premise that was wrong

`config export data` skips segments that were not enabled on the recording machine —
`src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131`:

```go
for _, segment := range block.Segments {
    if !segment.Enabled {
        continue
    }
```

So a fixture covers only what happened to be live when it was recorded, and every other segment
falls through `restoreData` (`src/config/segment.go:488-491`, returns `false`) into the live
`segment.writer.Enabled()` at `:243`.

| theme | segments configured | recorded | replay |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tokyo | 16 | 9 | 0.08s |
| atomic | 24 | 9 | 0.08s |
| jandedobbeleer | 17 | 8 | 0.07s |
| **chips** | 15 | 5 | **1.22s** |

The 1.22s is `wakatime` making a live HTTP request during what was supposed to be a replay.

The earlier "122/122 deterministic" measurement was an artifact: the fixture's `PWD` does not
exist, so every filesystem probe failed identically on both sweeps. It proves nothing.

## Verified facts

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `restoreData` returns before `writer.Enabled()` | `src/config/segment.go:203-205` vs `:243` |
| `Time.Format` is computed inside `Enabled()`, so replay renders it empty | `src/segments/time.go:27-28` |
| Pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` drops the whole rprompt block, silently | measured 419 → 328 bytes on `agnosterplus` |
| Adding `Format` restores it | measured 419 bytes, renders `10:41:00` |
| 53 of 102 `Enabled()` implementations assign template-visible state; ≥24 do I/O | scan |
| **The recorder skips disabled segments** | `src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131` |
| **124 themes, not 122** — 122 `.omp.json` plus 2 `.omp.yaml` | `ls themes/*.omp.*` |
| **65 themes carry a `time` segment** | `grep -l '"type": *"time"'` |
| **`date` renders in the renderer's local zone** | pinned `09:41:00Z` rendered `10:41:00` here |
| **`color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`** gates truecolor vs 256-colour | `src/terminal/writer.go:192`, read at `src/color/colors.go:312` |
| **`prompt.New` returns the session-cached config, ignoring the path** | `src/config/gob.go:44-49`, called from `src/prompt/engine.go:804-806` |
| **`--data` shipped in v29.35.3 and `data.mdx` documents partial hand-written files** | `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx:54-55` |
| **No bundled theme uses `<LINK>`** | `grep -l '<LINK>' themes/*.omp.*` returns 0 |
| `isHyperlink` is reset in neither `Write`'s prologue nor `String()`'s cleanup | `writer.go:78`, `:385-392`, `:605-619` |
| `DataKey` is the segment `Alias` or `Type` | `src/config/segment.go:412-418` |
| No theme PNG is tracked in git | `git ls-files 'website/static/img/themes/*'` → 0 |
| ns/op swings ~8x on this hardware; B/op and allocs/op are exactly stable | `-count=3` |
| `LoadData` reads only `env` and `segments`, tolerating unknown top-level keys | `src/config/data.go:43-90` |

Baseline to hold: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 9,150 B / 95 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 602 B /
14 allocs; `BenchmarkWritePlainASCII` 280 B / 6 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteSolid` 465 B / 16 allocs;
`BenchmarkWriteGradient` 1,762 B / 17 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteGradientChained` 789 B / 27 allocs.

## Decisions taken

- Ship Phase 2.0 alone, before the tokenizer refactor.
- **[R] Fix the recorder properly.** Record every configured segment with an explicit enabled
  flag; `restoreData` suppresses recorded-but-disabled segments without probing. Hermeticity has
  to be real before the harness or any render endpoint can lean on it.
- **[R] No breaking change.** Hand-written partial files keep working, with a warning and
  correctly derived state. `data.mdx:54` documents them and `--data` shipped in v29.35.3.

## Out of scope

The run stream, the SVG encoder, the tokenizer collapse, deleting `cli/image/`, the missing
`Plain` guard on OSC 8 emission, recording tooltip segments (`buildDataDocument` iterates
`cfg.Blocks` only, `config_export_data.go:127`), and changing the `DataKey` scheme.

**[R] Known limitation to document, not fix:** themes with two segments of the same type and no
`alias` collide on `DataKey` — the recorder already warns `multiple segments share the data key
"text"; the last one wins`. Goldens will encode that lossy behaviour. That is acceptable: the
harness is a change-detector, and the behaviour it locks in is the current one.

---

## Task A — make replay hermetic

**Owns:** `src/cli/config_export_data.go`, `src/config/data.go`, `src/config/segment.go`,
`src/cli/data.go`, `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx`, and their tests.

### A1. Record everything

Drop the `!segment.Enabled` skip. Record every configured segment, carrying its enabled state:

```json
{ "version": 1, "env": { … }, "segments": { "git": { "enabled": true, "data": { … } } } }
```

Shape is Task A's call, but the enabled flag must be per segment and must survive round-trip.
Keep backward compatibility with the current flat shape, since `website/segment_data.json` and
every user file use it.

`version` is safe to add: `LoadData` decodes the root into `map[string]json.RawMessage` and
reads only `env` and `segments`, so unknown top-level keys are already tolerated on the JSON,
YAML and TOML paths.

### A2. Suppress recorded-but-disabled segments

In `restoreData`:

- present and enabled → current behaviour: unmarshal the pinned data, `Enabled = true`, return
  `true`. No probe.
- **[R]** present and disabled → `Enabled = false`, `restored = true`, return `true`. **No
  probe.** This is the case that makes replay hermetic.
- absent → return `false` and fall through, as today.

**[R]** Do not move the recorded path's short-circuit. It sits at `:203`, before
`shouldHideForWidth` (`:212`) and the `runjobs` Job setup (`:227-241`). That bypass exists
today; changing it would change rendered output, and this phase's entire purpose is to
establish a baseline before output changes. File the width-hiding gap separately.

### A3. Warn and derive for unmarked files

A file without `version` is hand-written. Keep it working:

- Warn once per run, naming the file, saying it is neither hermetic nor deterministic, and
  giving the recorder command.
- For segments present in it, compute derived state so they stop silently vanishing.
- For segments absent from it, fall back to the live environment — the documented contract at
  `data.mdx:54-55`.

**[R] Where the derive happens matters.** Do **not** short-circuit at `:203` for this path.
Let `Execute` run normally so `Enabled()` fires at `:243` and then overlay the pinned data on
top. Short-circuiting at `:203` would skip `shouldHideForWidth` (`:212`), the `runjobs` Job
creation and its `defer` (`:227-241`) — so a pinned segment with a `timeout` would spawn live
child processes with no Job object, and `KillGoroutineChildren` could not terminate them on
Windows — and `segment.evaluated = true` at `:244`, leaving `renderFallback` (`:297`) dead.

Order is `Enabled()` then overlay, never the reverse. `json.Unmarshal` into the existing writer
preserves fields absent from the JSON, so pinned values win and derived values fill the gaps.

Add `--data-derive` to force this path for a recorded file too, for local debugging.

**[R] Note and document:** `restoreData` sets `Enabled = true` unconditionally, so a pinned
segment renders even where its live check would suppress it — `battery` on a machine without
one. That is today's behaviour and stays; say so in the docs rather than leaving it implicit.

### A4. Docs

Update `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx`: the recorder is the recommended path and the only
hermetic one; hand-written partial files still work and now derive correctly; the `version`
marker; the `alias` workaround for duplicate segment types.

**Verification:** `agnosterplus` with `{"time":{"CurrentDate":"2026-01-01T09:41:00Z"}}` renders
the time segment (it does not today). `chips` replayed from a re-recorded fixture makes **zero**
network calls and drops from 1.22s to the ~0.08s the other themes take. That timing is the
hermeticity proof — assert it, because the SSRF argument for any future render endpoint rests
on it.

---

## Task B — sanitized fixtures and the golden harness

**Owns:** the sanitizer, the harness test, the committed fixtures, and the `newEngine`
extraction below. Depends on Task A.

### B1. Sanitize structurally, not by string replace

**[R] A naive replace both corrupts and misses.** Case-insensitively replacing the username
rewrites `https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh` in recorded git data into
`aliceDobbeleer`; case-sensitively, it misses `C:\Users\Jande` and `%USERNAME%` in caps.

And the identity is not confined to the `env` block. Recorded fixtures carry:

- `Segment.Text` — the fully rendered string, e.g. `" jande@surface-pro "`
- `git.User.Name` / `git.User.Email` — the real git author identity
- `aws.AccessKeyID`; `az` `TenantID`, `HomeTenantID`, subscription IDs, `User.Name` (an email)
- `path.Folders[].Path`, `git.Dir`, `env.AbsolutePWD` / `PSWD` / `Folder` — absolute paths in
  both `C:\Users\x` and `/c/Users/x` forms, and `~/…` after tilde replacement
- `sysinfo` real memory and load; `battery` real charge state
- the hostname, which is often a device model

So: a `--sanitize` flag on the recorder that (a) overwrites the `env` identity keys with
`alice` / `contoso-devbox` / `~/dev/oh-my-posh`, matching `website/segment_data.json` so the
fixtures and the website tell the same story; (b) clears every `Segment.Text`, which is
recomputed on render anyway; (c) applies a per-field scrub list covering the above; (d)
normalises `sysinfo` and `battery` to fixed values.

Keep a backstop test asserting no fixture contains the current user, host or home path, and a
denylist test for `AccessKeyID`, `User.Email` and `TenantID`. The backstop is not the mechanism
— it is what catches the next person regenerating on their own machine, before it reaches a
public repo.

### B2. The harness

**[R] `TestMain` must neutralise three ambient inputs, or this fails on CI immediately.**
`code.yml` runs `go test ./...` on ubuntu, macos and windows.

1. `time.Local = time.UTC`. 65 themes render a `time` segment through
   `dateInZone(fmt, date, "Local")` (`src/template/date.go:44`). Runners are UTC; a European
   contributor regenerating goldens shifts 65 files by an hour. Setting `TZ` is not reliable —
   verified no effect on Windows.
2. Unset `TERM_PROGRAM` and `WT_SESSION`, or set `terminal.Program` / `color.TrueColor`
   explicitly, before `terminal.Init`. Otherwise macOS Terminal.app emits 256-colour and every
   golden fails.
3. Point `cache.Path()` at a temp dir, and do not call `cache.Close()`. `segment.isToggled()`
   (`:424-437`) reads `TOGGLECACHE` from the session cache and returns *before* `restoreData`,
   so anyone who has ever run `oh-my-posh toggle` gets different goldens.

**[R] Do not call `prompt.New`.** It calls `config.Get`, which returns the session-cached config
and ignores the path entirely (`src/config/gob.go:44-49`) — inside any real omp shell, that is
the developer's own config. But hand-rolling the Engine the way `config_export_data.go:78-81`
does skips everything `New` performs after `config.Get`: `terminal.Plain`, `forceRender`,
`prompt.Grow(512)`, `flags.HasExtra`, and `rectifyTerminalWidth` for xonsh/elvish/pwsh
(`engine.go:836-860`) — so those branches would have no coverage.

Extract the post-`config.Get` half of `New` into `newEngine(cfg *config.Config, env
runtime.Environment) *Engine`, call it from both `New` and the harness, and have the harness use
`config.Load(path)` directly.

Then, for each of the **124** themes — enumerate by the same extension set
`export_themes.mjs:18` uses, `.omp.json`, `.omp.toml` and `.omp.yaml`; the two YAML themes go
through a different unmarshal path (`Segment.UnmarshalYAML`, `segment.go:133-155`) that would
otherwise have zero coverage — render and compare byte-for-byte against a committed golden.

- Failure output: first differing byte offset plus a decoded escape context window. A raw diff
  of two ANSI blobs is unreadable, and this harness exists to be read during a refactor.
- Regeneration is one documented command, named in the failure message.
- Goldens capture current output. This phase changes rendering only for the derive path, so
  expect `time`-pinned cases to change and nothing else. **[R]** Generate goldens once, then
  re-run — a second-run diff means non-determinism survived and is a stop-and-report.

**[R] Cost to state up front:** `themes/**` is not in any `paths-ignore`, so every theme-touching
PR now regenerates goldens. Recent gradient work would have. That is the price of the net.

---

## Task C — the website pipeline

**Owns:** `website/export_themes.mjs`.

**[R] Do not try to record `website/segment_data.json`.** It is circular: reproducing it needs a
machine with AWS, Azure, GCP, kubectl, Terraform, Cloud Foundry, Firebase, Strava, Spotify and
YouTube Music all simultaneously live and authenticated. That is why it is hand-written, and its
synthetic values are the point.

Under A3 it keeps working and warns. Pass `--data-derive` explicitly from `buildPoshCommand`
(`export_themes.mjs:179-193`) to state the intent and silence the warning. One line.

**[R] Separately:** `exportTheme` (`:236-241`) treats any stderr as "skip this theme", returns
`null`, and `main` still exits 0 — so a broken data file yields a silently empty themes page
rather than a red build. And `.github/workflows/docs.yml:3-9` only runs on push to `main`, while
`code.yml` and `build_code.yml` carry `paths-ignore: ['website/**']`, so nothing validates this
at PR time. Make a non-zero exit a hard failure.

---

## Task D — reset `isHyperlink`

**Owns:** `src/terminal/writer.go` and its tests. Independent; any order.

`isHyperlink` (`writer.go:78`) is set at `:460`, `:503`, `:562` and cleared only by encountering
`<TEXT>` (`:508`, `:567`). It is absent from both reset points — `Write`'s prologue
(`:385-392`) and `String()`'s deferred cleanup (`:605-619`). An unbalanced `<LINK>` therefore
leaves it `true` for the process lifetime, and every later `Write` takes the branch at
`:700-703`: runes go straight to the builder with no length counting and no shell escaping. The
`serve` daemon makes "process lifetime" a real exposure.

Reset it with the other per-render flags. Add a unit test writing an unbalanced `<LINK>` and
asserting the next `Write` counts length correctly.

**[R]** The first draft claimed the golden harness proves this inert. It does not — no bundled
theme uses `<LINK>`. The unit test is the whole proof, and D has no ordering dependency on B.

---

## Landing order

`A` → `B` → `C`. B's fixtures need A's format; C needs A3 in place. `D` is independent.

## Verification (coordinator, not delegated)

1. `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` clean from `src/`, on more than this machine's default env.
2. **Hermeticity:** `chips` replayed from a re-recorded fixture drops from 1.22s to ~0.08s and
   makes zero network calls. This is the load-bearing claim.
3. All 124 goldens pass, including both YAML themes. Corrupt one fixture and confirm the failure
   names the theme and shows a readable escape window.
4. Run the harness with `TZ` set to something other than UTC and with `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`
   — both must still pass, proving `TestMain` neutralises them.
5. Run with `POSH_SESSION_ID` set to a live session, proving the harness ignores the session cache.
6. `agnosterplus` with only `CurrentDate` pinned renders the time segment; an unmarked file warns.
7. Grep every committed fixture for the current user, host, home path, `AccessKeyID`,
   `User.Email`, `TenantID` — zero hits.
8. Benchmarks against the baseline: allocs/op and B/op unchanged. Ignore ns/op.
9. `npm run themes` still produces images for a sample of themes, and now fails loudly when a
   theme errors.

machine (`src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131`, `if !segment.Enabled { continue }`).

Good catch on the restoreCache ordering — you were right to flag it rather than silently fix or ignore it. I verified it, and it's a real regression that needs fixing before this lands. Please do so now.

The problem, confirmed: `restoreCache` at `src/config/segment.go:206-209` returns early on a cache hit (when not streaming), which skips your `overlayData()` at `:245`. Before your change, a hand-written entry short-circuited at `:202` and its pinned data always won. Now a live cache hit beats the pinned data.

It's reachable, and awkwardly so — I checked every bundled theme for a segment that is both pinned in `website/segment_data.json` and carries a `cache` block. Exactly one hit: `themes/chips.omp.json` -> `wakatime`. That is the same theme we use as the hermeticity proof. So the website's chips image could render a cached live WakaTime value instead of the pinned one, non-deterministically.

This breaks the explicit constraint on this task: hand-written files must keep working exactly as documented. So it has to be fixed, not just noted.

Suggested shape, but use your judgement since you have the full context:

    cacheRestored := segment.restoreCache()
    if cacheRestored && !env.Flags().Streaming {
        segment.overlayData()
        return
    }

That keeps "pinned data wins" without falling through to a live probe, so it stays hermetic and matches the pre-change behaviour. Check whether `overlayData` is safe to call on a cache-restored writer — if the restored state and the pinned overlay interact badly, say so and propose something else rather than forcing this shape.

Please add a regression test that covers it directly: a segment with a `cache` block, a warm cache, and a hand-written data file pinning a different value — assert the pinned value wins. Without that test this will regress again the next time someone reorders Execute.

Then re-run what you ran before: `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, golangci-lint, and the chips timing check (it must stay at roughly 0.08s, not climb back toward 1.2s). Report the diff, the test, and the timing.

<result>All confirmed. Here's the summary of this fix.

## The fix

`src/config/segment.go`, `Execute()` — one line added plus a comment, at the `restoreCache` cache-hit branch:

```go
cacheRestored := segment.restoreCache()
if cacheRestored && !env.Flags().Streaming {
    // ... comment explaining why ...
    segment.overlayData()
    return
}
```

`overlayData()` is safe to call here: `json.Unmarshal(segment.pendingData, &segment.writer)` only touches fields present in the pinned JSON, leaving the cache-restored writer's other fields untouched (same in-place-interface-unmarshal mechanism already used elsewhere in this file), and it's a no-op when `pendingData` is empty — the common case, no hand-written override for that segment. `restoreCache()` already called `template.Cache.AddSegmentData` with the same writer pointer, so the in-place mutation is visible through that cache reference without a second `AddSegmentData` call.

## Regression test

Added `TestSegment_RestoreDataOverlaysOnTopOfACacheHit` in `src/config/segment_test.go`: warms the session cache for a `SESSION` segment with `SSHSession: false`, then runs `Execute` with a hand-written data file pinning `SSHSession: true`. Asserts the pinned value wins. The mock environment has no `Getenv`/`Platform` stub, so if the fix ever regressed to falling through to a live probe, the test would panic, not just fail silently.

I verified the test is load-bearing, not just passing by construction: temporarily reverted the one-line fix, reran the test — it failed (`the pinned value must win over the warm cache hit`) — then restored the fix and confirmed it passes again.

## Re-run results

- `go build ./...` — clean.
- `go test ./...` — clean, all packages pass including the new test.
- `golangci-lint run ./...` — 0 issues. `gofmt -l .` and `fieldalignment --fix ./...` — no changes needed.
- Chips timing, rebuilt binary, re-recorded fixture: **0.107s / 0.098s / 0.079s / 0.077s** across 4 runs — unchanged from before this fix (~0.08–0.11s), confirming the `restoreCache` change didn't reintroduce the ~1.2s wakatime network delay. That's expected: the hermetic recorded-and-disabled path in `restoreData` still short-circuits before `restoreCache` is ever reached for that segment.

`git diff --stat` now shows `src/config/segment.go` at +146/-16 and `src/config/segment_test.go` at +201/-1 (net of this fix's test addition), all other files unchanged from the prior report.</result>

git add -A src/cli src/config website/docs/configuration/data.mdx && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(config): make recorded data replay hermetic

The data recorder skipped segments that were not enabled on the recording
machine, so a recorded file only covered whatever happened to be live at the
time. Everything else fell through to a live probe on replay. Recording
themes/chips.omp.json captured 5 of its 15 segments, and replaying it took
1.2 seconds because the unrecorded wakatime segment still made an HTTP
request. Replay was neither fast nor reproducible, and could not be used as a
boundary against segments that take a URL from config.

Record every configured segment along with whether it was enabled, and skip
the probe entirely for one recorded as disabled. The same theme now records
14 of 15 and replays in under 0.1s. The remaining gap is two text segments
sharing a data key, which the recorder already warns about.

Replaying a hand-written file was also dropping any state a segment computes
in Enabled(). Pinning the time segment's CurrentDate rendered nothing at all,
because Format is derived there, and losing the only segment in a block took
the block with it. Hand-written files are documented and stay supported, so
they now run the segment first and apply the pinned values over the result,
which also keeps width hiding and the job setup for segments with a timeout.
A file with no recorder marker says so once, and points at the command that
produces one.

Pinned values also have to survive a warm cache, which returns before the
overlay would otherwise run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
Committed. Now the harness — with a design change that addresses the friction I flagged twice.

Rather than 124 full golden files (where any theme edit produces a large diff), I'll use a **hash manifest for breadth plus full goldens for a representative subset**. A theme change then touches one line instead of a whole file, while coverage stays complete and diffs stay readable where it matters.

input.prompt:
Repo: D:\oh-my-posh. Go module root is `src/` — run go commands from there, and ALWAYS use absolute paths when changing directory (cwd drift has already caused false results in this session).

Read the plan first: C:\Users\jande\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--oh-my-posh\6c0a282a-886f-458d-a426-93d95104b4a6\scratchpad\phase20-plan.md — implement "Task B — sanitized fixtures and the golden harness", WITH the design change below which supersedes the plan's "one golden file per theme".

Task A has already landed (commit b8381b97): the recorder now captures every configured segment with an enabled flag and a `version` marker, replay is hermetic, and `--data-derive` exists. Read `src/config/data.go`, `src/config/segment.go` and `src/cli/config_export_data.go` to see the current shape before designing anything.

## Design change: hash manifest + representative full goldens

Do NOT commit 124 full golden files. `themes/**` is in no workflow's `paths-ignore`, so every theme-touching PR would regenerate them and produce an unreadable diff.

Instead:
- **A hash manifest** covering all 124 themes: one line per theme, `<theme> <sha256-of-rendered-bytes>`, sorted. A theme change touches one line.
- **Full goldens for ~12 representative themes**, chosen to cover: both `.omp.yaml` themes (they use a different unmarshal path, `Segment.UnmarshalYAML` at `src/config/segment.go`), plain/powerline/diamond styles, a gradient theme, an rprompt theme, a theme with `<LINK>`-free hyperlink-adjacent markup if one exists, and the busiest theme by segment count. State your selection and why.
- Failure output must show, for a hash mismatch, the theme name and the regeneration command; for a full-golden mismatch, the first differing byte offset plus a decoded escape-sequence context window. A raw diff of two ANSI blobs is unreadable and this harness exists to be read during a refactor.
- Regeneration is ONE documented command, named in every failure message.

## Three ambient inputs that WILL break this on CI

`.github/workflows/code.yml` runs `go test ./...` on ubuntu, macos AND windows. `TestMain` must neutralise all three of these or the harness passes locally and fails in CI:

1. `time.Local = time.UTC`. 65 of 124 themes render a `time` segment via `dateInZone(fmt, date, "Local")` (`src/template/date.go:44`), so a pinned absolute instant still prints in the renderer's zone — pinning `09:41:00Z` renders `10:41:00` here. Setting the `TZ` env var does NOT work on Windows; assign `time.Local` directly.
2. Unset `TERM_PROGRAM` and `WT_SESSION` (or set `terminal.Program`/`color.TrueColor` explicitly) before `terminal.Init`. `color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal` (`src/terminal/writer.go:192`) gates truecolor vs 256-colour emission, so macOS Terminal.app produces different bytes.
3. Point `cache.Path()` at a temp dir and do NOT call `cache.Close()`. `segment.isToggled()` (`src/config/segment.go`) reads the session cache and returns before `restoreData`, so anyone who has run `oh-my-posh toggle` gets different output.

## Do not call prompt.New

`prompt.New` calls `config.Get`, which returns the SESSION-CACHED config and ignores the path entirely (`src/config/gob.go:44-49`) — inside a real omp shell that is the developer's own config, not the theme under test. But hand-rolling the Engine the way `src/cli/config_export_data.go` does skips what `New` performs after `config.Get`: `terminal.Plain`, `forceRender`, `prompt.Grow(512)`, `flags.HasExtra`, and `rectifyTerminalWidth` for xonsh/elvish/pwsh (`src/prompt/engine.go:836-860`).

Extract the post-`config.Get` half of `New` into a function taking an already-loaded config, call it from both `New` and the harness, and have the harness use `config.Load` directly. Verify `New`'s behaviour is unchanged.

## Fixtures must be sanitized structurally, not by string replace

A naive replace both corrupts and misses. Case-insensitively replacing the username rewrites `https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh` in recorded git data; case-sensitively it misses `C:\Users\Jande` and caps `%USERNAME%`. And identity is not confined to the `env` block — recorded fixtures carry `Segment.Text` (the fully rendered string, e.g. `" jande@surface-pro "`), `git.User.Name`/`User.Email`, `aws.AccessKeyID`, `az` TenantID/HomeTenantID/subscription IDs, `path.Folders[].Path`, `git.Dir`, `env.AbsolutePWD`/`PSWD`/`Folder`, real `sysinfo` memory and load, and real `battery` charge.

Add sanitization to the recorder (a flag) that overwrites the env identity keys with `alice` / `contoso-devbox` / `~/dev/oh-my-posh` — matching `website/segment_data.json` so fixtures and website tell the same story — clears every `Segment.Text` (recomputed on render anyway), scrubs the named fields, and normalises sysinfo/battery to fixed values.

Add tests asserting no committed fixture contains the current user, hostname or home path, and none contains `AccessKeyID`, `User.Email` or `TenantID`. That backstop is what catches the next person regenerating on their own machine before it reaches a public repo.

## Verify before reporting

- `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` clean from `src/`, golangci-lint clean (`src/.golangci.yml`).
- Generate the manifest, then re-run the harness: it must pass. Then re-generate a second time and confirm the manifest is byte-identical — if not, non-determinism survived, so STOP and report rather than papering over it.
- Run the harness with `TZ` set to a non-UTC zone AND with `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal` — both must still pass.
- Run with `POSH_SESSION_ID` set to something, proving the session cache is ignored.
- Corrupt one fixture and confirm the failure names the theme and shows a readable context.
- Confirm all 124 themes are covered (122 `.omp.json` + 2 `.omp.yaml`).
- Benchmarks unchanged: `go test -run=XXX -bench='BenchmarkEnginePrimary' -benchtime=200x -count=3 ./prompt/...`, baseline 9,150 B / 95 allocs. Gate on allocs and B/op; ns/op swings ~8x on this hardware, ignore it.
- Report how long the harness adds to `go test ./...`.

Report: files added/changed, your representative-theme selection and reasoning, the measured verification output, and anything in the plan that turned out to be wrong. Do not claim success for anything you did not run.

8 files: cloud-context, cloud-native-azure, devious-diamonds, and 5 more. The value is the machine owner's real email, from the Azure segment.

Two separate defects, and please fix both:

1. **The sanitizer misses it.** You scrub `az.User.Name`, but the recorded JSON serializes with lowercase keys — the actual path is `user.name` nested under the az segment's data. Your key-based scrub is matching on the Go field name, not the serialized key. Check every other field in your scrub list for the same mismatch; if `az.User.Name` was wrong, `git.User.Name`, `git.User.Email`, `aws.AccessKeyID`, `az.TenantID` and the rest may be silently no-ops too. I want to know which of your scrubs were actually doing anything, because a sanitizer that quietly does nothing is worse than none — it produces exactly the false confidence your backstop test was supposed to prevent.

2. **The backstop did not catch it.** It checks username, hostname, home path, and populated `AccessKeyID`/`TenantID`/`Email` — but this value sits in a field called `name`, so it slipped through. Make the backstop structural instead of field-name-based: walk every fixture's full JSON tree and assert no string value matches an email pattern, an absolute path pattern, the current user, or the current hostname — regardless of which key it sits under. That way the next field nobody thought of is caught by shape, not by having been enumerated in advance.

Then regenerate all 124 fixtures, re-run the whole harness, and confirm:
- zero fixtures contain the real email, any other email that is not the synthetic `alice@contoso.com`, or any absolute path
- the new structural backstop FAILS if you hand-edit one fixture to reintroduce an email, and passes once reverted — verify it is load-bearing, do not assume

content.text:
Holding the commit. **Your real email address is in 8 of the 124 fixtures**, at `segments.az.data.user.name`, from the Azure segment.

The sanitizer scrubs `az.User.Name` — the Go field name — but the recorded JSON serializes lowercase, so the actual path is `user.name` and the scrub silently did nothing. The backstop test missed it because it checks specific field *names* (`Email`, `AccessKeyID`, `TenantID`), and this value lives under a key called `name`.

I found it by walking every fixture's JSON tree rather than grepping for the fields the sanitizer claims to handle. That distinction is the whole lesson here: a sanitizer verified against its own field list will always pass.

Sent back with two requirements — fix the key-casing mismatch (and audit whether the *other* scrubs were no-ops for the same reason), and rebuild the backstop to be **structural**: walk every string value in every fixture and reject anything shaped like an email, an absolute path, the current user, or the current hostname, regardless of key. Enumerated field lists only catch what someone already thought of.

Everything else about the harness verified clean:

- 124 fixtures, 12 goldens, 124 manifest lines, none gitignored
- Manifest byte-stable across three regenerations
- Passes under `TZ=Pacific/Auckland`, `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`, and a fake `POSH_SESSION_ID`
- Recolouring one `tokyo` segment fails at byte offset 33 on both the golden and the hash, naming the regen command

The agent found two real things on its own worth keeping: `template.Init` only rebuilds the global cache when nil, so rendering 124 themes in one process silently reused the first render's identity until it called `ResetCache()` — caught by the regenerate-twice check I'd required. And `manifest.sha256` matched the repo's `*.sha256` gitignore rule, so the manifest would never have been committed at all. A safety net that isn't in the repo is the most expensive kind of fake.

# Phase 2.1 — One tokenizer

Collapse the three hand-maintained copies of the same scanner in `src/terminal/writer.go`
into one. No run stream, no SVG, no behaviour change except the drift bug below.

## Why now, with evidence

`writer.go:895-902` documents that `writeBody`, `writeBodyGradient` and `countVisibleCells`
must walk text with "the exact same tokenization rules". They do not. Measured:

```
input:  ab<transparent,transparent>hidden</LINK>tail
VisibleCells() = 6        (counts "ab" + "tail")
rendered length = 2       (renders "ab")
```

`countVisibleCells` (`:945-966`) has no `hyperLinkEnd` case. `</LINK>` therefore falls to
`default`, which recomputes `invisible = match.FG == transparent && match.BG == transparent`.
Both are empty for `</LINK>`, so invisible flips back to false and the tail is counted.
`writeBody`/`writeBodyGradient` (`:529`, `:590`) have an explicit `hyperLinkEnd` case that
only consumes the token, so `isInvisible` survives — which is the documented long-standing
behaviour, pinned by `TestWriteGradientInvisibleSpanExcluded`
(`writer_gradient_test.go:423-446`, "isInvisible persists past `</>`").

The count feeds `color.GradientCells`, so a segment whose template contains an invisible span
followed by `</LINK>` gets its gradient interpolated over the wrong number of cells.

That is the justification. Not SVG — this is a live bug caused by the duplication.

## The three copies, precisely

| | lines | differs from `writeBody` by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `writeBody` | `:492-545` | — |
| `writeBodyGradient` | `:551-598+` | `writeVisibleRune` instead of `write`; `stampGradient()` and `cellIndex += 4` in the `hyperLinkTextEnd` case |
| `countVisibleCells` | `:903-972` | emits nothing; keeps `hyperlink`/`invisible` in locals rather than package globals; no `hyperLinkEnd` case (the bug) |

Everything else — the `s != '<'` fast path, `scanAnchor`, the `match.ok` fallback, the five
anchor cases, the `hyperlinkTextPosition` no-text fallback of 4 — is duplicated verbatim.

## Constraints

- **Byte-identical ANSI for all 124 bundled themes**, except where the drift fix legitimately
  changes a gradient cell count. Any golden change must be explained and justified segment by
  segment, never blanket-regenerated.
- **Allocations must not regress.** `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 95 allocs/op, 9,150 B/op;
  `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 14 / 602; `BenchmarkWritePlainASCII` 6 / 280; `BenchmarkWriteSolid`
  16 / 465; `BenchmarkWriteGradient` 17 / 1,762; `BenchmarkWriteGradientChained` 27 / 789.
  Gate on allocs/op and B/op only — ns/op swings ~8x run to run on this hardware.
- **No closures over per-call state in the hot path.** A callback-per-token design will heap
  allocate the closure and blow the allocation gate. This is the single most likely way to
  fail.
- `write()` is called per rune for every prompt on every keypress. Treat it accordingly.

## Design

A cursor struct with a `next()` method, shared by all three consumers:

```go
type token struct {
    Anchor string   // "" for a literal rune
    FG, BG string
    Rune   rune
    Size   int      // bytes consumed
    Kind   tokenKind
}
```

Each consumer keeps its own loop and its own actions; only the scanning and classification
move into the cursor. A struct with a pointer receiver and no escaping references stays on
the stack, so no allocation. Verify that with `-gcflags=-m` and the benchmarks, not by
assumption.

Do **not** unify the three consumers' *actions* behind a mode enum or an interface. The
actions genuinely differ (emit / emit+stamp / count-only), and the state they mutate differs
(package globals vs locals). Unifying scanning is the win; unifying actions reintroduces
branching in the per-rune path for no benefit.

## Tasks

### Task A — extract the cursor

Introduce the cursor and rewrite the three consumers against it, preserving current behaviour
**including the drift bug**. This step must be provably inert: all 124 goldens byte-identical,
every existing terminal test passing unchanged, allocations flat.

Landing the extraction and the bug fix separately is the whole point — if a golden moves in
Task A, the extraction is wrong.

### Task B — fix the drift

Give `countVisibleCells`'s consumer the `hyperLinkEnd` case the others have, so `</LINK>`
consumes without touching invisibility. Add the case above as a regression test asserting
`VisibleCells(txt)` equals the rendered length.

Expect goldens to move only for themes that actually contain an invisible span followed by
`</LINK>`. Report which themes moved and why; if none move, say so — the bundled themes may
not exercise it, and the unit test is then the only proof.

### Task C — the sibling defects, only if trivially safe

`writer.go:700-703` emits OSC 8 hyperlink sequences with no `Plain` guard, unlike every other
escape emitter in the package. Fix only if it leaves all 124 goldens unchanged (it should —
goldens are not rendered with `Plain`), and add a test asserting `Plain` suppresses hyperlink
escapes. If it moves a golden, stop and report instead.

## Verification (coordinator, not delegated)

1. `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` clean.
2. All 124 goldens byte-identical after Task A. This is the gate.
3. Benchmarks after each task: allocs/op and B/op against the baseline above.
4. `go test -run=XXX -bench=. -benchtime=200x -count=6 ./terminal/...` before and after, compared
   with benchstat on allocs.
5. The drift case renders and counts consistently after Task B.
6. `TZ=Asia/Tokyo TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal` — harness still passes.
7. Escape-emission ordering is unchanged: the existing byte-exact tests in `writer_test.go`,
   `writer_hyperlink_test.go` and `writer_gradient_test.go` must pass **without edits**. If any
   expected string needs changing, that is a behaviour change and must be justified, not
   accommodated.

## Out of scope

The run stream, SVG, de-globalizing the 28 package variables, `isInvisible`'s persistence past
`</>` (long-standing, pinned by tests, and changing it is a user-visible behaviour change), and
the `Write`-prologue leading-anchor special case at `:411-428`.

# Phase 2.1 — One anchor classifier

Remove the duplicated anchor-handling switch from the three scanners in
`src/terminal/writer.go`. No run stream, no SVG.

**Revision 2.** The first draft proposed a per-rune cursor, gated on allocations, and called the
124 goldens the gate. All three were wrong. Changes marked **[R]**.

## Why, with evidence

`writer.go:895-902` documents that `writeBody`, `writeBodyGradient` and `countVisibleCells`
walk text with "the exact same tokenization rules". They do not:

```
ab<transparent,transparent>hidden</LINK>tail
VisibleCells() = 6      (counts "ab" + "tail")
rendered length = 2     (renders "ab")
```

`countVisibleCells` (`:945-966`) has no `hyperLinkEnd` case, so `</LINK>` falls to `default`,
which evaluates `invisible = match.FG == "transparent" && match.BG == "transparent"` — i.e.
`"/LINK" == "transparent"` — and flips invisibility back off. The other two consume the token
without touching it (`:529`, `:590`).

An exhaustive 3-token differential over a 15-token alphabet (3,375 inputs) found **29 body-loop
divergences, all 29 containing `</LINK>`, and nothing else.** So this is the only drift between
the three loops.

The count feeds `color.GradientCells` (`:445`, `:456`), the collapse decision
(`prompt/engine.go:416`) and `backgroundEdge` (`:526`). A wrong count moves all three.

### **[R]** The larger, related divergence

The same differential with a leading anchor allowed found **86 divergences**, of which the
leading-anchor prologue alone caused more than everything else combined:

```
<transparent,transparent>ababtail
VisibleCells() = 8      rendered length = 0
```

`Write` consumes a leading anchor in its prologue (`:418-436`) and then calls
`countVisibleCells(body, …)` at `:441` — which starts with `invisible = false` regardless of
what that anchor was. This needs only a fully-transparent leading override; the `</LINK>` case
additionally needs `<LINK>` markup, which no bundled theme and no config I can find uses. So
this class is strictly more reachable and is the same bug.

Both are in scope. The first draft declared this one out of scope without noticing it was the
bigger half.

## The three copies

| | lines | differs from `writeBody` by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `writeBody` | `:492-545` | — |
| `writeBodyGradient` | `:551-606` | `writeVisibleRune` not `write`; `stampGradient()` and `cellIndex += 4` in `hyperLinkTextEnd` |
| `countVisibleCells` | `:903-972` | emits nothing; state in locals not globals; no `hyperLinkEnd` case |

## **[R]** Design — share the classifier, not the loop

The first draft proposed a `token` struct from a `next()` method per rune. That was measured
against three alternatives, all 0 allocs/op, medians over `-count=6..8`:

| shape | 80-char plain | ~800-char mixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| today (`s != '<'` inline, `scanAnchor` only on `<`) | ~78 ns | ~1780 ns |
| **first draft's `next()` returning `token`** | ~480 ns (**6.1x**) | ~4400 ns (2.5x) |
| cursor holding state, `next() bool` | ~232 ns (3.0x) | ~3200 ns (1.8x) |
| **shared `classifyAnchor`, fast path left inline** | ~90 ns (1.1x) | ~1740 ns (1.0x) |

The cost is not the struct copy — `next()` is too large to inline, so the fully-inlined
`s != '<'` fast path becomes a call per rune. `write()` runs per rune per prompt per keypress.

**So: keep `if s != '<' { … }` and the `i` bookkeeping inline in all three loops. Extract only
what happens after a `<` — `scanAnchor` plus the five-case classification — into a shared
helper.** That is where the drift lives and it is cost-neutral.

**[R] Index ownership stays with the consumers.** `writeBody`/`writeBodyGradient` do
`i = writeAnchorOverride(match, background, i)` (`:538`, `:599`), and for `</>` that reaches
`endColorOverride` (`:1148`), which compares `position == textLen` against the package global
`textLen`, set only by `Write` at `:473`. `countVisibleCells` never sets it. A shared helper
that owned `i` would silently change that comparison. Do not let it.

## **[R]** Precondition — the goldens are not the gate

Measured statement coverage of `src/terminal` during `go test ./prompt/ -run TestGoldenThemes`:

```
writeBody          81.8%
countVisibleCells  85.3%
writeBodyGradient   0.0%
writeVisibleRune    0.0%
stampGradient       0.0%
```

Zero, because no bundled theme uses a gradient (`golden_test.go:117-120`), uses `<LINK>`, or
uses `transparent,transparent`. The terminal package's own tests reach `writeBodyGradient` at
only 34.3% — the entire anchor switch at `:568-597`, including `stampGradient(); length += 4;
cellIndex += 4`, is untested. An implementer could delete `cellIndex += 4` and every gate in the
first draft stayed green.

**Task 0 is therefore a precondition, not an afterthought.**

## Tasks

### Task 0 — characterize before touching anything

Add tests covering `writeBodyGradient`'s five anchor cases on a gradient segment: `<LINK>`,
`<TEXT>`, `</TEXT>` (both with and without text, asserting the 4-cell stamp advance and
`cellIndex += 4`), `</LINK>`, `<>`, and a colour override mid-gradient. Also cover
`writeVisibleRune` and `stampGradient`.

**Gate: `writeBodyGradient`, `writeVisibleRune` and `stampGradient` at 100% statement
coverage before Task A begins.** These tests must pass against today's code unchanged — they
describe current behaviour, including the drift. If one fails on today's code, that is a
finding: stop and report it rather than adjusting the test.

Re-record the benchmark baseline on the executing machine and commit the raw benchstat output.
The first draft's numbers do not reproduce (`BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 596 not 602 B/op,
`WriteSolid` 460 not 465, `WriteGradient` 1756 not 1762, `WriteGradientChained` 781 not 789),
because they were taken at `-benchtime=200x`, which is too short to be stable.

### Task A — extract the classifier

Rewrite the three consumers against the shared classifier, preserving behaviour **including
both drift bugs**. Provably inert: all 124 goldens byte-identical, all existing terminal tests
passing **unedited**, Task 0's new tests passing unedited, and benchmarks within noise on both
allocs/op and ns/op.

If a golden moves in Task A, the extraction is wrong.

### Task B — fix both divergences

1. Give the counting consumer the `hyperLinkEnd` case, so `</LINK>` consumes without touching
   invisibility.
2. Seed the count with the leading anchor's invisibility: `Write` knows at `:418-436` whether
   the consumed leading anchor was fully transparent, and must pass that into the pre-pass the
   way it already passes `startHyperlink`.

Regression tests: `VisibleCells(txt)` equals rendered length for both cases above. Verified
compatible with the existing `TestVisibleCells` (`writer_gradient_test.go:245-264`) and
`TestWriteGradientInvisibleSpanExcluded` (`:423-446`) — neither should need editing.

Goldens should not move: no bundled theme uses `<LINK>` or `transparent,transparent`. If one
does move, stop and report — it means a theme reaches this and the change is user-visible.

### Task C — **[R]** Plain and hyperlinks, respecified

The first draft's version would have corrupted output. Guarding only the escape emitters is
wrong because `write()` takes the `isHyperlink` branch at `:709-712` — `builder.WriteRune(s);
return` — **before** the `!Interactive && !Plain` check at `:718`. Measured with only the
emitters guarded:

| | output | `length` | visible chars |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| today | `\x1b]8;;http://www.google.be\x1b\google\x1b]8;;\x1b\` | 6 | 6 |
| emitters guarded only | `http://www.google.begoogle` | 6 | **26** |

The URL streams in as literal text, uncounted, and every width consumer downstream is wrong.
And the first draft's proposed test would have passed on that.

So: in `Plain` mode suppress the OSC 8 wrappers **and** the URL runes — `write()` must return
early when `isHyperlink && Plain`. Test asserts the full Plain render of a `<LINK>` is exactly
`"google"` with `length == 6`.

Emission sites are `:469`, `:513`, `:519`, `:531`, `:572`, `:578`, `:592`. (The first draft
cited `:700-703`, which is the control-rune comment inside `write()`.)

Task C is independent of A and B. Land it separately.

## Verification (coordinator, not delegated)

1. `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` clean.
2. Coverage precondition met before Task A; re-measured after.
3. All 124 goldens byte-identical after Task A.
4. **[R]** Benchmarks with `-benchtime=2s -count=10`, compared with benchstat on **ns/op and
   allocs/op**. At `-benchtime=2s` ns/op is stable to ±2% on this machine (1192/1213/1241);
   the first draft's "ns/op swings 8x, ignore it" was an artifact of `-benchtime=200x` and
   would have hidden the 6.1x regression the first draft's own design introduced. Run against
   both `./terminal/...` and `./prompt/...` — `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` lives in `prompt`.
   Treat B/op as advisory: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` varies ±30 B run to run.
5. Both drift cases render and count consistently after Task B.
6. Existing byte-exact tests in `writer_test.go`, `writer_hyperlink_test.go`,
   `writer_gradient_test.go` pass **without edits**. Any expected string needing a change is a
   behaviour change to justify, not accommodate.

**[R] Dropped:** the first draft's `TZ`/`TERM_PROGRAM` verification step. `golden_test.go:58`
sets `time.Local = time.UTC` and `:64` unsets `TERM_PROGRAM` unconditionally, so that step
passes regardless of what the refactor does.

## Out of scope

The run stream, SVG, de-globalizing the 28 package variables, and `isInvisible` persisting past
`</>` — long-standing, pinned by tests, and changing it is user-visible.

plain mode. The link wrappers were written straight to the buffer, so a plain
render still carried them.

Suppressing only the wrappers makes it worse. The URL between the opening tag
and the text streams through the rune writer while the hyperlink flag is set,
and that path returns before anything is counted, so the address itself would
appear as visible text that the length does not account for: twenty extra
columns for a short URL, and every consumer of the width then disagrees with
the screen. Suppress the URL as well.

content.text:
Phase 2.1 is complete — `beaa7160` landed, and the mutation test confirmed the new test catches the naive version of the fix (`"http://www.google.begoogle"` instead of `"google"`).

Now your question, which is a fair challenge. I measured rather than defended the decision.

**You're mostly right.** Of 1,049 segment entries across the 124 fixtures, there are only **63 unique keys, and 51 of them are byte-identical in every theme** — pure duplication, 510 KB of it.

**But a single shared file can't work outright.** 12 keys genuinely differ per theme, because the recorder captures state *derived from that theme's segment properties*:

| key | distinct values |
|---|---|
| `time` | 66 |
| `git` | 39 |
| `executiontime` | 10 |
| `status` | 8 |
| `text` | 7 |

`time` is the clearest case: `Format` is computed inside `Enabled()` from each theme's `time_format` property, so 66 themes record 66 different values. That's the same mechanism as the bug we fixed in `b8381b97` — derived state is theme-specific. `git` varies with `fetch_status` and `fetch_upstream_icon` changing which fields get populated.

`website/segment_data.json` gets away with one file only because it's hand-written and *doesn't* carry derived fields — which is precisely why it silently drops segments.

**The hybrid is clearly better than what I built:**

| layout | size |
|---|---|
| current, 124 files | 510 KB |
| shared base + per-theme overrides | **156 KB** (15 KB base + 141 KB deltas) |

427 override entries instead of 1,049. Roughly a third the size, and adding a theme adds a small delta rather than a whole 4 KB fixture.

**Honest answer to "why didn't we":** I didn't evaluate it. The plan said "record a data file per theme" because that's the natural output shape of `config export data`, and I carried it forward without asking whether the harness needed per-theme granularity. It doesn't — the harness only needs determinism and change-detection.

Worth doing, but as its own change rather than folded into 2.1, since it touches the fixtures every golden depends on. Want me to take it now, or move on to 2.2?
If this is only meant as an intermediate state and we delete all of those files once we're done, then it's okay for me and we don't need to refactor this.

They're not intermediate — that's my fault for not being clear.

The golden harness is the permanent regression suite for theme rendering. The fixtures are its inputs, so they stay for as long as the goldens do. Phase 2.2 adds an SVG encoder alongside ANSI; it doesn't retire the ANSI goldens, which are exactly what protects the hot path we just refactored.

So the 510 KB is permanent, and every new theme adds another ~4 KB fixture on top.

Given that, your decision rule points the other way. My recommendation: do the consolidation now, before 2.2 builds anything on top of the fixture layout — it's ~30 minutes, drops to 156 KB, and the shared base makes it obvious at a glance which 12 segments are theme-dependent and why.

But it's genuinely low stakes either way, and 510 KB of JSON is not a real problem. If you'd rather keep momentum on the renderer, I'll leave it and note it as a known cleanup.

input.summary: Merge rule should pick richest, not most common
input.message:
Good work, and your root-cause analysis of the git split was correct and well-evidenced. But the merge rule needs changing before this lands, and your own findings are what show why.

`mergeMostCommon` picks the value recorded by the most themes. For `git` that selected the 53 themes that never fetch status, so the committed fixture now has `Ahead: 0`, `Behind: 0`, `BranchStatus: ""`, empty `Working`/`Staging`, empty upstream. The consequence is that the goldens no longer exercise git status rendering at all — ahead/behind, working-tree counts, upstream icon, branch status formatting. That is the most complex template logic in the project and the most-used segment, so the harness just lost its most valuable coverage while looking green.

Most-common is the right rule for "what does a typical machine look like". It is the wrong rule for a test fixture, where more populated fields means more template branches exercised. A theme that does not fetch status simply never references those fields, so richer data is harmless to it.

I verified the fix is safe before asking you to make it. Taking your merged fixture and swapping only the `git` entry for the richer variant (the one with `Ahead: 16`, `BranchStatus: "↑16"`, `Working.Modified: 2`, `Untracked: 5`):
- all 124 themes still render non-empty
- still 124 pairwise-distinct outputs
- `chips` renders `next ↑16   (?5 ~2)` again instead of a bare `next`

So: change the merge rule from most-common to richest. Suggested definition, but use your judgement — for each key, choose the variant with the greatest number of populated leaf values, counting a leaf as populated when it is not the zero value for its type (non-empty string, non-zero number, true, non-empty array/map). Break ties deterministically, and keep the tie-break stable across runs so regeneration stays byte-identical.

Apply it to every key, not just `git`. Your own numbers show `time` has 66 variants, `executiontime` 10, `status` 8, `text` 7, `path` 4, `sysinfo` 4 — each is a chance to pick data that exercises more of a template rather than less.

Then re-run everything you ran before, and additionally report:
- for each of the 12 multi-variant keys, which variant the new rule picked and how many populated fields it has versus what most-common picked
- confirm all 124 still render non-empty and still produce 124 distinct outputs
- confirm regeneration twice in a row is byte-identical, since the tie-break must be deterministic
- the count of themes whose output changed versus the current committed state, with an explanation

If the richest rule turns out to pick something absurd for a particular key — data that no real machine would produce and that makes a theme render nonsense — say so and special-case it rather than shipping it silently.

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys

PUA = []


def is_pua(cp):
    return 0xE000 <= cp <= 0xF8FF or 0xF0000 <= cp <= 0xFFFFD


ESC = re.compile(r"\\u([eEfF][0-9a-fA-F]{3})|\\U000([fF][0-9a-fA-F]{4})")

glyphs = set()
per_theme = {}

for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "themes", "*.omp.*")):
    raw = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    found = set()

    for ch in raw:
        if is_pua(ord(ch)):
            found.add(ord(ch))

    for m in ESC.finditer(raw):
        hexpart = m.group(1) or m.group(2)
        cp = int(hexpart, 16)
        if is_pua(cp):
            found.add(cp)

    glyphs |= found
    per_theme[os.path.basename(path)] = len(found)

print("distinct PUA codepoints across all bundled themes:", len(glyphs))
print("themes using at least one:", sum(1 for v in per_theme.values() if v))
top = sorted(per_theme.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:5]
print("busiest themes:", ", ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in top))

# Powerline separators live in E0B0-E0D4; everything else is icon territory.
powerline = {c for c in glyphs if 0xE0A0 <= c <= 0xE0D4}
print("powerline separators/branch glyphs:", len(powerline))
print("other icons:", len(glyphs) - len(powerline))

That settles the font question for the gallery: a woff2 subset of ~246 glyphs plus Latin is on the order of tens of kilobytes, against the 8 MB of PNGs it replaces. The strategy splits by destination:

| destination | font approach |
|---|---|
| `--format svg` locally | reference the family by name; the user has the Nerd Font installed |
| theme gallery | inline `<svg>` in the page + site-hosted subset woff2 |
| shareable single file | embed a subset as data URI, sized to the glyphs actually used |
| GitHub README | PNG — GitHub sanitizes SVG and strips `<style>`, so fonts can't load at all |

The catch: 246 is the *bundled* set. An arbitrary user config can reach any of ~10,000 Nerd Font glyphs, so the shareable case needs subsetting driven by the actual render rather than a fixed list — which the run stream gives us for free, since it knows exactly which runes were emitted.

`writeColorise` (`writer.go:762-768`) guards only `IsEmpty()` and `IsGradient()`. Every payload originates from `color.String.ToAnsi` or `ansiFromColorful`:

| Form | Produced at | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `30`–`37`, `39`, `90`–`97` (fg) / `40`–`47`, `49`, `100`–`107` (bg) | `color/colors.go:332-338` via `ansiColorCodes` `color/colors.go:245-263` | a colour *name* (`red`, `lightBlue`, `default`) |
| `38;2;r;g;b` / `48;2;r;g;b` | gookit `TplFgRGB`/`TplBgRGB`; reached from `color/colors.go:310-313` (`#RRGGBB` + `TrueColor`) | hex colour, truecolor mode |
| `38;2;r;g;b` / `48;2;r;g;b` | `color/colors.go:211-217` (`SetAccentColor`), returned at `color/colors.go:281-291` | `accent` keyword — **always truecolor, ignores `TrueColor`** |
| `38;2;r;g;b` / `48;2;r;g;b` | `ansiFromColorful` `color/gradient.go:399-413` | gradient cell, truecolor mode |
| `38;5;n` / `48;5;n` | `color/colors.go:306-307` (`C256`) | a bare numeric string `0`–`255` — **always 256, regardless of `TrueColor`** |
| `38;5;n` / `48;5;n` | `color/colors.go:316` (`style.C256()`) | hex colour, `TrueColor == false` — **the downgrade** |
| `38;5;n` / `48;5;n` | `color/gradient.go:395-397` | gradient cell, `TrueColor == false` — the gradient downgrade |
| `38;5;n` / `48;5;n` | `color/colors.go:319-322` — dead code (`ParseUint` at 301 already handled it) | — |
| `48;…` from a `38;…` | `Ansi.ToForeground()` `color/colors.go:128-134` (used `writer.go:1116`, `1208`) and `Ansi.ToChannel()` `color/colors.go:138-149` (used `writer.go:928`) | channel conversion; prefix-string rewrite only, base-16 codes pass through **unconverted** |
| `""` | many `ToAnsi` failure paths (`colors.go:267`, `303`, `325`) | guarded out at `writer.go:763` |
| raw `linear-gradient(...)` | `ToAnsi` passes gradients through untouched (`colors.go:275-279`, `colors.go:355-357`) | guarded out at `writer.go:763` |
| literal `"transparent"` | `ToAnsi` passes it through (`colors.go:271-273`) | **not guarded by `writeColorise`.** All colour-emitting call sites guard with `IsTransparent()`/`IsClear()` except `writer.go:1291` (`if previousFg != fg && !previousFg.IsGradient() { writeColorise(previousFg) }`), which only checks `IsGradient`. A history entry can hold `Foreground: "transparent"` (added at `writer.go:1198` before the transparent branch returns at `writer.go:1212`), so `\x1b[transparentm` is reachable in principle. |

The `transparentStart` form is separate: `writeTransparentStart` (`writer.go:774-780`) emits `\x1b[0m\x1b[<fg-payload>;49m\x1b[7m` — the *background* rendered as a foreground code plus reverse video (`writer.go:105-106`).

**The 256-colour gate**: `color.TrueColor` (`color/colors.go:30`), set exactly once at `writer.go:258` — `color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`, where `Program` comes from `getTerminalName()` (`writer.go:273-285`, reads `TERM_PROGRAM` / `WT_SESSION`).

**Can a caller force truecolor?** Yes, but only globally and only by assignment: `color.TrueColor` is an exported package var with no setter and no per-call parameter. `terminal.Init` must run first (it overwrites it). Two caveats if flipped mid-process:
- `color.Cached.ToAnsi` (`color/colors.go:385-398`) keys on `cachedColorKey{colorString, isBackground}` (`colors.go:380-383`) — **`TrueColor` is not in the key**, so already-cached hex→`38;5;n` entries would be served stale. `Cached` is on by default (`config/config.go:90-93`, disabled only by `OMP_CACHE_DISABLED=1`).
- `gradientCellCache` *does* include it (`color/gradient.go:351-353`), so gradients are safe.
- Existing precedent for forcing it: `prompt/golden_test.go:76-81` unsets `TERM_PROGRAM`/`WT_SESSION` before `terminal.Init` rather than assigning the var.

## 3. Natural capture points

Everything below is package-level mutable state in `writer.go:44-92`; rendering is single-threaded.

### A. `Write` prologue — `writer.go:438-559`
In scope: `background`/`foreground` params (usually the keywords), `backgroundColor`/`foregroundColor` (SGR, after line 443), `CurrentColors`+`ParentColors` (**hex**), the full `txt`, the consumed leading `match` (raw hex in `match.FG`/`match.BG`), `bgGradientCells`/`fgGradientCells` (after line 535), `gradientRenderCells` (line 515) and `isHyperlink`/`isTransparent`/`isInvisible`.
Missing: **run boundaries** — inline `<...>` overrides inside `body` change colour mid-segment and are not visible here; **attributes**; **cell width for non-gradient segments** — `countVisibleCells` only runs when a channel is a gradient (`writer.go:513-514`). Width is obtainable by bracketing the call with `Len()` (`writer.go:681-683`), or by calling `VisibleCells(txt)` (`writer.go:1083-1088`), but not from a local.
Verdict: gives one run per `Write`. Correct only for anchor-free, non-gradient fragments — which is most separators/diamonds but not most segment texts.

### B. `writeBody` loop — `writer.go:565-618` / `writeBodyGradient` — `writer.go:624-679`
In scope: `txt` (the body) and `i` (byte offset) → **exact run boundaries**; the `background` param; `backgroundColor`/`foregroundColor`; `currentColor` (`color.History`, `writer.go:57`) whose top is the active override; `activeBackground()`/`activeForeground()` helpers (`writer.go:895-909`); `isInvisible`/`isHyperlink`/`isTransparent`.
The `anchorOverride` case (`writer.go:610-612` and `writer.go:671-673`) is *exactly* the colour-change boundary; `anchorHyperlinkStart/Text/TextEnd/End` (`writer.go:584-606`) are the hyperlink boundaries. A run flush before each `writeAnchorOverride` call plus one at loop exit covers the whole segment.
Missing: **attributes** (style anchors never reach these cases — they are consumed inside `writeAnchorOverride` at `writer.go:1164-1173` and written straight to the builder); **width** (recoverable as a `length` delta across the run, since `write()` maintains `length` at `writer.go:811`); in gradient mode the colour changes **per cell**, so a "run" here is one cell wide unless the encoder collapses.
Verdict: **the smallest complete set for text + colour + boundaries, minus attributes.**

### C. `write(s rune)` — `writer.go:782-823`
In scope: the rune, `isInvisible` (783), `isControlRune` filter (792), `isHyperlink` (801), `Plain`, and `runewidth.RuneWidth(s)` computed at line 811 — **the only place cell width per rune exists in the non-gradient path**. Colour reachable via `activeBackground()`/`activeForeground()`.
Missing: run grouping; attributes. Per-rune cost.

### D. `writeVisibleRune` — `writer.go:845-857`
Gradient path only (called from `writeBodyGradient` at 632 and 676). In scope: rune, `visible` flag (846), `cellIndex`, `runewidth.RuneWidth(s)` (855), and via `stampGradient` the exact per-cell payload. **The only place the per-cell gradient colour and the rune it applies to are simultaneously in scope.**
Missing: attributes; grouping.

### E. `stampGradient` — `writer.go:865-879`
In scope: `bgGradientCells[clampCellIndex(...)]` / `fgGradientCells[...]` (the per-cell payloads), `isTransparent`, `activeBackground()`/`activeForeground()`.
Missing: the rune (written by the caller *after*), the width, attributes. Also **early-returns** when `isTransparent` (868-870) or when the channel is overridden (872, 876) — so it does not fire for every cell. Unsuitable as the sole hook.

### F. Colour-change event sites (complete set)
`writeSegmentColors` `writer.go:1090-1153` (segment base colour established, `currentColor.Add` at 1152), `writeAnchorOverride` `writer.go:1155-1250` (`currentColor.Add` at 1198), `endColorOverride` `writer.go:1252-1326` (`currentColor.Pop` at 1258/1269/1299). These three are where the effective pair changes; combined with `write()` for width they are the exhaustive colour event stream.

**Minimum viable set:** `Write` prologue (segment open) + `writeBody`/`writeBodyGradient` `anchorOverride` case and loop exit (run flush) + `write()` or `Len()` deltas (width) + `writeVisibleRune` (gradient per-cell) + `Write:555-558` (segment close). Attributes require three *additional* sites — see §4.

## 4. Attribute state — confirmed: none exists

Verified against current `writer.go`.

- The package var block `writer.go:44-92` contains no attribute/style variable. Full list: `BackgroundColor`, `CurrentColors`, `ParentColors`, `Colors`, `Plain`, `Interactive`, `builder`, `length`, `foregroundColor`, `backgroundColor`, `currentColor`, `textLen`, `bgGradientCells`, `fgGradientCells`, `cellIndex`, `gradientRenderCells`, `isTransparent`, `isInvisible`, `isHyperlink`, `Shell`, `Program`, `progressTerminals`, `formats`, `escapePrefix`, `escapeSuffix`.
- `knownStyles` (`writer.go:30-39`) is a static `[]*style` of literal escape pairs. Only three sites write them, all fire-and-forget `writeEscapedAnsiString`:
  - `writer.go:502` — leading style anchor consumed in `Write`'s prologue.
  - `writer.go:1166` — `style.AnchorEnd` → `style.End`.
  - `writer.go:1170` — `style.AnchorStart` → `style.Start`.
- Contrast with colour, which has a real stack: `currentColor color.History` (`writer.go:57`, type at `color/colors.go:58-106`) with `Add`/`Pop`/`Background`/`Foreground`, pushed at `writer.go:507`, `1152`, `1198` and popped at `558`, `1258`, `1269`, `1299`.
- `String()`'s reset defer (`writer.go:686-701`) resets `isTransparent`/`isInvisible`/`isHyperlink`/gradient state — nothing style-related, because there is nothing.
- `</>` does **not** clear attributes: `writeAnchorOverride:1158` routes `resetStyle.AnchorEnd` to `endColorOverride` (`writer.go:1252-1326`), which touches colours only. So `<b>x</>y` leaves bold on for `y`.
- The only style awareness in the file is the local closure `isStyleOrReset` inside `countVisibleCells` (`writer.go:1009-1021`) and the loop at `leadingAnchorInvisible` (`writer.go:242-246`) — both exist purely to exclude style anchors from the *invisible* computation, and neither records anything.
- Attributes cannot leak across `Write` calls in the **byte stream** because line 555 emits `resetStyle.End` (`\x1b[0m`) at the end of every `Write`. There is no in-memory counterpart to that reset.

**What capturing attributes would require:**

1. A package-level attribute state next to `currentColor`, e.g. `activeStyles [len(knownStyles)]int` — **counters, not booleans**. `<b><b>x</b></b>` currently emits `1m 1m 22m 22m`; a bool set would turn bold off at the first `</b>`, diverging from the bytes. Nesting depth per attribute is the only way to mirror the emitted stream.
2. Mutation at exactly the three emission sites: `writer.go:502` (increment), `writer.go:1170` (increment), `writer.go:1166` (decrement).
3. Reset at `Write`'s entry (alongside the per-segment resets at `writer.go:451-466`) **and** in `String()`'s defer (`writer.go:686-701`), to mirror line 555's `\x1b[0m`.
4. Deliberately **no** mutation in `endColorOverride` — `</>` must not clear attributes, matching current behaviour.
5. Index by `knownStyles` slot, not by SGR code: `<b>` and `<d>` **share the End code `\x1b[22m`** (`writer.go:31` and `writer.go:36`). A code-keyed model cannot tell them apart; the emitted bytes genuinely cannot either. Note also `<r>` reverse uses `\x1b[7m`/`\x1b[27m` (`writer.go:38`), which collide with the transparent-rendering mechanism (`transparentStartSuffix` `writer.go:106`, `transparentEnd` `writer.go:108`, set/cleared at `writer.go:1126`, `1221`, `1275-1278`, `1307`) — an attribute model must distinguish an explicit `<r>` from transparent rendering, which `isTransparent` already tracks separately.
6. `Plain` mode (`writer.go:721-723`, `739-741`) suppresses all of these escapes; the state machine must run regardless of `Plain` if the run stream is to be correct when `Plain` is set.

Full attribute inventory (`writer.go:30-39`): `<b>` 1/22, `<u>` 4/24, `<o>` 53/55, `<i>` 3/23, `<s>` 9/29, `<d>` 2/22, `<f>` 5/25, `<r>` 7/27.

**This is the part that makes it non-trivial** — everything else is reading existing state; attributes require inventing new state and deciding nesting/reset semantics that the current code has never had to define.

## 5. Cost of a disabled capture

**Measured `Write` calls per prompt.** Every non-empty `Write` emits exactly one `\x1b[0m` (`writer.go:555`), and the goldens are rendered with `shell.GENERIC` (no escape wrapping), so counting resets in `D:\oh-my-posh\src\prompt\testdata\goldens\*.golden` gives the exact count:

| theme | Write calls | | theme | Write calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| avit | 4 | | jandedobbeleer | 15 |
| agnoster | 10 | | chips | 16 |
| tiwahu | 10 | | powerlevel10k_rainbow | 18 |

**4–28 per primary prompt, median ~15.** Add a handful more for RPrompt/tooltip/transient (separate passes through `extra.go:78`, `extra.go:199`).

**Guard placement and frequency:**
- Per-`Write` guard (`writer.go:438`, `555`): **4–30 branch tests per prompt.** Free.
- Per-run guard (before `writeAnchorOverride` at `writer.go:611`/`672`, plus loop entry/exit): call it 2–5× the above, so **~20–150 per prompt.** Still free.

Guarded by benchmarks: `D:\oh-my-posh\src\terminal\bench_test.go:10` and `:24`, `D:\oh-my-posh\src\terminal\gradient_bench_test.go`, `D:\oh-my-posh\src\prompt\bench_test.go`.

## 6. Segment and block identity

**All `terminal.Write` call sites** (no package outside `src/prompt` calls it):

| Site | Fragment | Engine knows |
|---|---|---|
| `engine.go:210` | block filler | the filler template only; `e.blockTailColors`. **No segment.** Called from `shouldFill`, itself called from `writeBlock` (`engine.go:285`, `300`) |
| `engine.go:552` | segment text (Plain/Powerline) | `e.activeSegment` |
| `engine.go:561` | leading diamond | `e.activeSegment` (+ `e.previousActiveSegment` for the edge colour) |
| `engine.go:562` | segment text (Diamond) | `e.activeSegment` |
| `engine.go:566` | segment text (Accordion) | `e.activeSegment` |
| `engine.go:606` | trailing diamond, final | `e.activeSegment` |
| `engine.go:616` | previous trailing diamond (diamond→diamond) | both |
| `engine.go:621` | previous trailing diamond | both |
| `engine.go:643` | leading powerline symbol | both |
| `engine.go:674` | powerline separator (inverted) | both |
| `engine.go:678` | powerline separator | both |
| `extra.go:78` | secondary/transient/debug/valid/error prompt | `*config.Segment` (`prompt`) local, not `e.activeSegment` |
| `extra.go:199` | right template | same local |

**Segment identity available:** `*config.Segment` → `Name()` (alias, else Title-cased type — `config/segment.go:164-176`), `DataKey()` (`segment.go:453-459`), `Type` (`config.SegmentType`), `ResolveStyle()` (`segment.go:426-434`), `Alias`. Separator writes straddle two segments (`writeSeparator` `engine.go:592-679` reads `e.previousActiveSegment` → `e.activeSegment`); note `renderActiveSegment:548` calls `writeSeparator(false)` **after** `setActiveSegment` has already advanced `e.activeSegment`, so during a separator write `activeSegment` is the *upcoming* segment.

**Block identity:** *not* in scope at any `Write` call site.
- `*config.Block` reaches `writeSegment(block, segment)` (`segments.go:184`) and `renderBlockSegments(results, block, executed)` (`segments.go:65`), but `renderActiveSegment` (`engine.go:547`) and `writeSeparator` (`engine.go:592`) take no block and read none.
- The render ordinal lives only as the loop variable `i` in `primary.go:105` (`for i, block := range blocks`) and is not stored on `Engine` (struct at `engine.go:21-50` has `allBlocks` but no current-block field).
- `config.Block.Index` exists (`config/block.go:35`) but is a config/merge field consumed by `Block.key()` (`block.go:38-44`), not a render position — it is 0 for most configs.

**Is there an existing parameter that could carry it?** No. `Write(background, foreground color.Ansi, txt string)` (`writer.go:438`) has no identity argument, and adding one would touch all 13 call sites.

The established pattern in this codebase is a **package-level push next to the colour push**, not a parameter: `terminal.Interactive = segment.Interactive` (`engine.go:394`), `terminal.SetColors(...)` (`engine.go:429`), `terminal.SetParentColors(...)` (`engine.go:572`). A `terminal.CurrentSegment`/`CurrentBlock` set in `setActiveSegment` would follow that shape exactly — but it would be stale or absent for the filler write (`engine.go:210`, no segment at all), for the separator/diamond writes (which belong between two segments), and for the `extra.go` prompts (which never call `setActiveSegment`).

## 7. Existing structured output — prior art

**Yes, one direct precedent, and it works by re-parsing bytes rather than capturing.**

`D:\oh-my-posh\src\cli\image\image.go` (the PNG exporter, driven by `cli/config_export_image.go:135-157` which feeds it `eng.Primary()`):

content.text: Correction to what I told you earlier, and it makes 2.2 substantially easier. **I said semantic colour is destroyed before anything is written. That's wrong.** `CurrentColors` and `ParentColors` hold hex for the entire duration of `Write` and are never overwritten — only the *derived* package vars are SGR. Inline anchors carry raw hex in `match.FG`/`match.BG` too. So a run stream can carry real colour without reparsing SGR at all. `asAnsiColors` resolves keyword → palette → SGR in three stages; capture takes the value after stage two. Usage across the bundled themes also narrows the scope sharply: | feature | themes | |---|---| | inline colour anchors `<#hex,…>` | **67** | | any style anchor | **5** (all ``) | | gradients | **0** | So run boundaries from inline anchors are the thing that must be right. Attributes affect 5 themes and only bold — and they're the expensive part, needing new nesting-counter state at three sites, because `x` emits `1m 1m 22m 22m` and ``/`` share the `22m` terminator. Two more latent bugs surfaced, worth recording separately from this work: - **`image.go` has no 256-colour patterns at all** — only truecolor and base-16. A render on Apple Terminal (where `TrueColor` is false) loses colour entirely in the PNG. - **`color.Cached.ToAnsi` doesn't include `TrueColor` in its cache key**, so forcing truecolor mid-process serves stale downgraded entries.

input.content: # Phase 2.2a — Capture a run stream Capture styled text runs alongside the ANSI byte stream, so an encoder can consume structure instead of re-parsing escapes. No SVG yet, no deletions. ## The correction this plan rests on Earlier analysis claimed semantic colour is destroyed before anything is written. **That is wrong.** `CurrentColors` and `ParentColors` (`writer.go:45-47`, set via `SetColors` `writer.go:287` and `SetParentColors` `writer.go:298`) hold `#RRGGBB` / colour name / palette value for the whole of `Write` and are never overwritten. Inline overrides carry raw hex in `match.FG` / `match.BG` (`writer.go:142-147`, live at `:507` and `:1175`). Only the derived package vars `backgroundColor` / `foregroundColor` are SGR, assigned at `writer.go:443`. `asAnsiColors` (`:1328-1354`) runs three stages — keyword resolve, palette resolve, `ToAnsi`. **Capture takes the value after stage two.** No SGR reparsing, no lossy inverse of the 256-colour downgrade, no base-16 table inversion. That is the difference between this and `cli/image/image.go`, which reconstructs colour by scanning finished bytes through 20 prefix-overlapping regexes in non-deterministic map order. ## Measured scope | feature | bundled themes using it | | --- | --- | | inline colour anchors `<#hex,…>` | **67** of 124 | | any style anchor | **5** (all ``) | | gradients | **0** | Run boundaries from inline anchors are the case that must be correct. Attributes are rare in bundled themes but not in user configs, and they are the expensive part — see "Deferred". ## Cost budget Measured `Write` calls per primary prompt: 4 (avit) to 28 (night-owl), median ~15. Visible cells 144–323. content.text:
That review invalidates my plan's core design, and it's right. Let me be direct about what it found.

**The design can't work as written.** Three findings compound:

- **Run text isn't reconstructible at run granularity.** `write()` both *drops* runes (invisible, control, Plain-mode URL) and *rewrites* them (zsh `%`→`%%`, bash `\`→`\\`). Source-slicing is therefore wrong, and builder-slicing is wrong too because a run's byte span contains escapes I wasn't flushing on. The only exact route is appending per rune — the cost my plan explicitly forbade.
- **Capture point 1 is wrong for 52 of 124 themes.** `writeSegmentColors` replaces the colour pair with `currentColor`'s top *before* emitting anything, so capturing in the prologue records the segment's colour for text rendered in the anchor's colour.
- **Gradient runs can't carry hex at all.** `GradientCells` returns ready-to-print SGR, so that capture point can only produce the exact form Task B says never to invert — and per-cell capture means 300–2000 runs per prompt, blowing the budget the whole design rested on.

Plus: my correctness bar was unachievable (the filler is rendered *once* through `Write` then `strings.Repeat`-ed by the engine, so the run stream can never match the prompt text), my verification would have covered almost nothing (`shell.GENERIC` has a nil escape map; 0 gradients, 0 `<LINK>` in the fixtures — the same 0%-coverage shape as the last round), and deferring attributes is both **cheaper than I claimed** (an 8-slot counter is O(runs), not O(runes)) and **more damaging** — `image.go` renders five attributes today, so an attribute-less stream can't replace it, which blocks the SVG encoder rather than deferring it.

**The root cause is that I drifted from the architecture we agreed.** The original note said the run stream should sit *between resolver and encoder — a sibling to the ANSI encoder, not a consumer of its output*. What I planned was capture bolted onto the ANSI writer, which is why every finding above is a symptom of reading state that the byte stream has already consumed.
